To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quantitative detection of single RNA molecules is possible in living cells, and that it is a powerful tool to study gene expression.
the number of RNA molecules per cell is highly variable, even between cells of the same type, and that the number of mRNA molecules in the cell is a key determinant of the cell's behavior.

1) single‐molecule detection assays have become a powerful tool to study gene regulation; 2) single‐molecular techniques can be used to study RNA molecules in their cellular context; 3) single‐molecules are not distributed randomly in cells, they are organized into subcellular domains; 4) RNA molecules can be counted with single‐molecule techniques; and 5) RNA numbers are highly dynamic and are subject to rapid regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How does the cell know what genes to transcribe and what to translate? What are the mechanisms by which the cell controls the expression of genes and how do these control mechanisms interact?
the molecular mechanisms of gene regulation in eukaryotes
the quantitative analysis of gene expression at the single‐molecule level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the single‐molecule approach to gene expression has been a major breakthrough in our understanding of gene expression, and it is a powerful tool in the hands of the biologist.
single‐molecule nucleic acid detection has been and continues to be a transformative technology in biology.
the number of mRNA molecules per cell is not a static, constant value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand how the spatial and temporal organization of cells and tissues arises from the spatial and temporal control of transcription.
we have been trying to understand the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control gene expression.
single‐molecule techniques are now the standard in the field of gene expression, and that they have become a powerful tool for the quantitative study of the molecular basis of gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the single‐molecule approach is the most powerful way of quantifying gene expression.
cells are not average but are highly distinct and dynamic individuals with greatly and rapidly changing gene expression, whose behavior can be measured, modelled, predicted, and finally comprehended.
cells are not average individuals but are highly distinct, with great and sudden changes in gene expression, and that this behavior can be measured, predicted, and comprehended.
